pages.text: A process can also talk to players while it runs. Three built-in functions do this, called with CALL like any other function:
$(li)$(l)PRINT$() writes text on screens.$(li)$(l)INPUT$() reads a value into a variable.$(li)$(l)WRITE$() puts a value into an I/O block as a variable item.

The devices for this are display blocks, laptops, tablets and I/O blocks. Bind each of them to a program and function, like a trigger block. Display blocks next to each other form one big screen.$(br2)COLOR changes the colors of the text that follows. The constants COLOR_BLACK to COLOR_WHITE name the 16 colors:

$(1)PROGRAM hello$(br)NOOP$(br)FUNCTION greet$(br)BEGIN$(br)  CALL CLS$(br)  CALL COLOR$(br)    PARAMETER foreground COLOR_YELLOW ;$(br)    PARAMETER background COLOR_DARK_BLUE ;$(br)  CALL PRINT$(br)    PARAMETER value "Process " ;$(br)  CALL PRINT$(br)    PARAMETER value PID.pid ;$()
$(1)  CALL COLOR$(br)    PARAMETER foreground COLOR_WHITE ;$(br)END FUNCTION$()
INPUT takes a matching item from an I/O block first. Otherwise it waits until a player types a line on a laptop or tablet. The handbooks Functions and Devices describe all of them.
